idiom_name: factory functions / static factory class compiled into the test target
implementation_notes: C++ has no framework-provided object mother: GoogleTest supplies TEST_F fixtures for per-suite setup only, while cross-suite canned objects are ordinary factory functions or a 'struct CustomerMother' with static members compiled into the test target. C++20 designated initializers plus default member initializers replace the mother for flat aggregates (Customer{.name = "Ada", .tier = Tier::Vip}), so keep the classic factory for deep graphs, ownership-heavy types and classes whose constructors enforce invariants. Place the mother in the test target's own namespace/library so production code cannot depend on it.
pitfalls: Returning by value is right, but a mother that hands out pointers or references to one shared static object reintroduces exactly the aliasing bug the pattern is meant to avoid.
Designated initializers require aggregate types and designators in declaration order (C++20); for a class with a validating constructor the mother still has to call the real constructor.
Helper functions defined in headers without 'inline' produce duplicate-symbol linker errors as soon as two test translation units include the mother.
Copying a fixture into a test copies whatever its members own; if the domain type manages resources by raw pointer, the copy is unsafe - say so in the mother's contract or return unique_ptr.
